TennisScore LED · live demo

The court-side scoreboard you run from your phone

Two LED panels, a small controller and the umpire's phone. No internet and no app to install: the scoreboard makes its own Wi-Fi. Tap the team that won the point and the board, and every spectator's phone, updates at once.

LED scoreboard · 64 × 64 LEDs · 2 panels P5

Start screen
Plays before the first point.
Auto demo: a full match plays by itself. Tap the phone to take over.

Umpire's phone · the real app

This is the actual app. Tap a team to give it the point, or open Configure for names, rules and clocks.

What it does

Built and tested on real panels at a club court, in daylight and at night.

Its own Wi-Fi

Switch it on and join the TennisScore network. Works on any court, with or without mobile signal. The board itself shows how to connect.

Wi-Fi “TennisScore” → 192.168.4.1

One tap per point

Points, games, sets and tie-breaks are counted by the rules you pick. A wrong tap is fixed with Undo, point by point.

Undo up to 40 points back

Spectators follow live

Anyone on the court Wi-Fi can open the match on their own phone and watch the score change.

up to 8 phones live

The moments that matter

DEUCE, DECIDING POINT, BREAK POINT, GAME POINT, SET POINT and MATCH POINT appear on the board in place of the team name, in a coloured frame.

40 blinks at a deciding point

Who serves

Pick the first server once. A ball on the board shows who serves, and it moves by itself after every game and every 2 points in a tie-break.

tap “… serves” to correct

Match statistics

Every point is logged. Points won on serve and return, break points, service games held, a momentum chart with one dot per game and a one-line story, and the last 300 finished matches.

see the example below

Share the result

One tap makes a result picture for WhatsApp or Instagram, or a short text summary. After the match the board itself shows a STATS card too.

picture 1080 × 1350

The board keeps the score

The scoreboard holds the match itself. If the umpire's phone locks or loses Wi-Fi, it catches up with the board when it comes back.

nothing lost when a phone sleeps

Winner ceremony

Trophy, the winning team or club in rainbow letters, the final score, and fireworks every 20 seconds.

until the next match starts

Readable in the sun

Day mode uses full, saturated colours and high brightness. Night mode is softer. Brightness can be set from the phone.

brightness 5 – 255

A clock between matches

Flip clock, big digital, analog, a tennis-court clock, and prayer times for cities in Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia.

time comes from the phone

Doubles and clubs

Two names per team (long names scroll), and an optional club name per team for the winner screen.

e.g. ARIF - BAYU
Next version

Handheld remote

Score without taking out your phone: an M5StickS3 remote with two buttons and a small screen. A = point team 1, B = point team 2, hold A = undo. Try the preview next to the board above.

M5StickS3 · 2 buttons · 1.14″ screen

Match statistics

The real stats page from the umpire's phone. It fills in live during the match and keeps the finished matches. Touch the momentum chart, open a match from the history, try Save image, or delete a match (tap Delete twice).

Example names are made up. Serve, return and break point numbers appear when the umpire picks who serves.

20 start screens

Before the first point the board plays pixel-art animations, shuffled or one fixed favourite. Click one to put it on the board above.

Match rules

Set once in Configure before the match. The board follows them automatically.

SetsBest of 1, 3 or 5
Games per set1 to 10 (6 by default)
SetWin by 2 games with a tie-break at games-all, or first to the number of games (6-5 ends it, no tie-break)
Tie-breakFirst to 1 – 12 points, win by 2 (7 by default)
DeuceAdvantage (standard) · one advantage, then a deciding point · deciding point at the first 40-40 (no-ad)
ServeOptional: pick who serves first, the board follows the order (also in tie-breaks)
CorrectionsUndo point by point (up to 40 points back), or set any score by hand

Hardware

Standard parts, so a broken panel or cable is easy to replace.

Display
2 outdoor-grade P5 LED panels (HUB75, 64 × 32 each) stacked to 64 × 64 LEDs, about 32 × 32 cm. One-panel version (64 × 32, about 32 × 16 cm) available.
Controller
ESP32-S3 with 16 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM. Remembers its settings when switched off.
Power
5 V. Runs from a USB power bank at the court, or from a 5 V adapter.
Remote
Next version, optional: M5StickS3 (ESP32-S3, 1.14″ screen, 2 buttons, built-in battery). Talks directly to the scoreboard by radio, no phone in between.
Phone
Any phone with a web browser: Android or iPhone. Nothing to install.
